event_date_text: Shutterstock Shutterstock Calendar Get the latest on UNESCO activities worldwide Home All events Statutory meetings Informal meetings Events DG's schedule Other events Jump to : Next international days Calls for applications and statutory deadlines This Month at UNESCO International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists 2 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France) UNESCO marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, calling for stronger action to ensure accountability for crimes committed against journalists worldwide and to bring perpetrators to justice. Under the tagline “Threats Evolve. Impunity Endures”, this year's campaign highlights the alarming findings of UNESCO's latest report on the safety of journalists. Exhibition: A Shared Blue Heritage 2 November – 31 December 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), on fences Marking the 25th anniversary of the UNESCO Convention on the Protection of the Underwater Cultural heritage, this photo exhibition celebrates the richness of our shared underwater heritage and highlights the importance of protecting it for future generations. It offers a glimpse into the history of humanity beneath the waters. International Day against Violence and Bullying at School, including Cyberbullying 5 November 2026 This year, the Day will be observed under the theme “Every learner safe and well: From promise to practice.” It highlights a whole school approach to safety and well-being, encompassing violence prevention, mental health and psychosocial support, teacher support, inclusion and digital safety. 2026 Award Ceremony of the UNESCO-Equatorial Guinea International Prize for Research in the Life Sciences and Fellowship Programme for Young Women Scientists in Africa 5-6 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), Rooms I, II, Hall Pas Perdus UNESCO will mark the 10th edition of the UNESCO-Equatorial Guinea International Prize for Research in the Life Sciences and the 2nd edition of the Fellowship Programme for Young Women Scientists in Africa with this two-day celebration. FMSTAN 10th Anniversary Symposium: “Reinventing science diplomacy in a changing world 9 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 9:15am-7pm, Room XI (Hybrid) The Foreign Ministries Science & Technology Advice Network (FMSTAN) is convening this event to examine how science diplomacy can foster peace amid growing pressures on multilateralism, while amplifying emerging voices shaping the future of global cooperation. The event takes place in the context of the World Science Day for Peace and Development (10 November) and constitutes an official side event of the Paris Peace Forum (10-11 November). COP31 - 2026 UN Climate Change Conference 9-20 November 2026 (Antalya, Türkiye) This year’s COP31 is centred on water and ocean resilience. UNESCO is advocating for integrated solutions, drawing on its interdisciplinary mandate spanning science, education, the safeguarding and promotion of local and Indigenous knowledge systems, and culture. UNESCO will also host several side events, including the launch of a report on how artificial intelligence shapes our perception and understanding of climate change. 4th Chief Science Advisors Roundtable: Trusted Advice in a World of Plural Knowledge 10 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 9am-5pm (open morning session), Room XI (Hybrid) Under the theme “Trusted advice in a world of plural knowledge”, the session will reflect a twofold challenge: Widening the set of voices that can legitimately inform government decision-making, within and across countries, and sharpening the procedures by which contested evidence is weighed and made visible. Open Science for Innovation Conference 12 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 9:30am-6:30pm, Room XI Convened in the context of the 25th anniversary of World Science Day for Peace and Development (10 November), the conference will examine how open science partnerships can support the implementation of the UNESCO Recommendation on Open Science. Award Ceremony for the 15th Edition of the UNESCO-Madanjeet Singh Prize for the Promotion of Tolerance and Non-Violence - International Day for Tolerance 16 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 6pm-7.30 pm, Room I UNESCO will host the 15th award ceremony of the Madanjeet Singh Prize for the Promotion of Tolerance and Non-Violence on this day, marking the International Day for Tolerance. The Prize rewards outstanding contributions in the fields of science, the arts, culture and communication fields aimed at the promotion of a spirit of tolerance and non-violence. International Symposium: Integrating Marine and Underwater Cultural Heritage into Ocean Governance: achievements and future priorities 16 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 10 am-5.30 pm, Room II The symposium is part of a series of activities to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the 2001 Convention on the Protection of the Underwater Cultural Heritage. This milestone provides an important opportunity to take stock of the Convention’s achievements while looking ahead to the challenges and opportunities shaping the future of underwater cultural heritage (UCH) protection and management. Concert: HAMACA — Songs Suspended Between Peru and France 18 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 7-9 pm, Room I Christine Audat presents HAMACA, a creation between France and Peru that brings together soloists, choir, orchestra and audience in a participatory musical experience. World Philosophy Day 19 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 6:30-20:30 pm, Room II On World Philosophy Day, UNESCO will bring together thinkers and decision-makers at its Headquarters for a lecture by philosopher Souleymane Bachir Diagne. Entitled “Living the Earth Together”, the lecture will explore the concept of the Universal Human. A round-table discussion will follow the lecture, centered on a fundamental question “Thinking and acting together: philosophy to inhabit a world with plural challenges.” Launch of the 2026 Global Report on Early Childhood Care and Education – 2nd Edition 19-20 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 9 am-6 pm, Rooms I and X On World Children’s Day, UNESCO will unveil the second edition of the biennial Global Report on Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE), Financing for equitable and inclusive access to quality ECCE, jointly published by UNESCO, UNICEF and OECD. Across the two days, participants will discuss the Report’s key findings and recommendations, share approaches and solutions for financing ECCE, and identify concrete actions to advance equitable and inclusive access to quality ECCE in support of the Sustainable Development Goals. 5th Anniversary of the Inscription of Congolese Rumba on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage List No web page yet 23-27 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), Rooms I, IX, Cinema This 5-day celebration will highlight Congolese Rumba as a shared cultural heritage of the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, its transmission to younger generations and its contribution to intercultural dialogue and a culture of peace. Event will include exhibition, film screening, three thematic panels, a main high-level celebration, as well as a public dance workshop and documentary screening. UNESCO Campus XL – Film screening “Alboran, an Ocean as our Heritage" 24 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 10am-12:30pm, Room I The Campus will include a preview screening of the documentary “Alboran, an Ocean as our Heritage", which dives into the heart of this threatened ocean crossroads, reminding us that the ocean is neither a backdrop nor a mere resource, but a heritage to pass on and protect. Through debates, exchanges, and testimonies, students will be invited to explore the ocean’s richness and the threats its faces, and to reflect on their role in its protection. Premiere screening – Documentary “Alboran, an Ocean as our Heritage" 24 November 2026 (UNESCO HQ – Paris, France), 7:30pm, Room I Alexis Rosenfeld and 1OCEAN invite you to the premiere of the documentary "Alboran, an Ocean as our Heritage" produced as part of their ongoing project with UNESCO. Through striking underwater imagery, the film conveys a clear message: the ocean is neither a backdrop nor merely a resource. It is a shared heritage that we must protect and pass on to future generations. This message lies at the heart of UNESCO’s work for the ocean. After the screening, the film’s team will take part in a discussion about the making of the documentary and the issues it raises. 21st session of the Intangible Cultural Heritage Committee 30 November – 5 December 2026 (Xiamen, China) The Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, meeting in Xiamen, will examine the nominations of 64 elements submitted by 82 countries who join forces to safeguard living heritage across borders. This includes 18 nominations submitted jointly by several countries, twice as many as last year, demonstrating a growing commitment to safeguarding living heritage that is shared across borders and strengthens ties among communities. It also includes potential first inscriptions for four African countries and a nomination from a Small Island Developing State (SIDS). event_date_text: About UNRWA Toggle submenu Mandate and History Toggle submenu Mandate History Mandate and History UNRWA is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East. The United Nations General Assembly established UNRWA in 1949 with a mandate to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to registered Palestine Refugees in the Agency’s area of operations pending a just and lasting solution to their plight. Principles and Values Toggle submenu Humanitarian Principles Sustainable Development Goals Principles and Values As an Agency with a humanitarian mandate – to assist and protect Palestine Refugees – humanitarian principles provide the space to make our work possible. From ensuring the sanctity of our shelters in times of crisis, to maintaining access to the most vulnerable populations, to advocating on behalf of Palestine Refugees, the principles of humanity , impartiality , neutrality , and independence are at the heart of all UNRWA operations. Leadership Toggle submenu Our leadership Organisational structure Leadership UNRWA is led by a Commissioner-General, appointed by the UN Secretary-General. The Commissioner-General is supported by a Deputy Commissioner-General for Programmes and Partnerships and a Deputy Commissioner-General for Operational Support. Funding Toggle submenu How we are funded How we spend funds Our partners Funding UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions, mostly from government donors. Accountability Toggle submenu Colonna Report Advisory Commission Internal oversight Ethics office Dispute Tribunal Work with us Toggle submenu Careers Procurement Key areas of work What we do UNRWA’s key services include education, healthcare, relief and social services, infrastructure and camp improvement, microfinance, and emergency response. event_date_text: UNESCO UNESCO General Conference The General Conference is the highest governing body of UNESCO. Home President 43rd Session Documents Previous Sessions Secretariat The General Conference determines the policies and the main lines of work of the Organization Its duty is to set the programmes and the budget of UNESCO. It also elects the Members of the Executive Board and appoints, every four years, the Director-General. The working languages of the General Conference are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish. The General Conference consists of the representatives of UNESCO's Member States. It meets every two years, and is attended by Member States and Associate Members, together with observers for non-Member States, intergovernmental organizations and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). Each country has one vote, irrespective of its size or the extent of its contribution to the budget. event_date_text: SOUTHMOD at 10: Evidence Before Action 14 September 2026, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia | Ten years after the launch of SOUTHMOD , UNU-WIDER brings together government officials, researchers, and members of the SOUTHMOD network to celebrate and reflect on the programme's achievements; and explore its future role in supporting evidence-based policymaking across the Global South. Drawing on a decade of experience, the event examines how tax-benefit microsimulation can help governments design more effective, equitable, and data-driven policies. Read more Can Africa escape the climate–conflict–poverty trap? 30 September 2026, Helsinki, Finland | Climate change increasingly reshapes development prospects around the world, but the risks are especially acute in countries where livelihoods remain closely tied to rain-fed agriculture, state capacity is limited, and conflict risk is already high. On 30 September 2026, distinguished economist Edward Miguel delivers WIDER Annual Lecture 30, Can Africa escape the climate–conflict–poverty trap? In this lecture, Edward Miguel examines how rising temperatures, economic stress, and armed conflict interact to produce a vicious cycle that threatens long-term development, with a particular focus on Africa. Read more 2026 Jobs and Development Conference 9–10 October 2026 in Hong Kong, China | The Jobs and Development Conference 2026 brings together researchers, policymakers, and practitioners from around the world to discuss the latest insights on jobs, labour markets, and inclusive development. The conference is co-organized by the World Bank, UNU-WIDER, and the International Labour Organization (ILO), in partnership with the Development Policy Research Unit (DPRU) at the University of Cape Town, the Institute for Structural Research (IBS) in Poland, and hosted by the Institute for Emerging Market Studies (IEMS) at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST).
